title: Consensus degradation with sentence length

net_line.label: e + d (net)
net_line.note: per-tercile e + d, computed from the two series above

source.rows: regime=R_AB, dim=words_tercile, rule=MAJ (cells T1, T2, T3)
source.definitions: e = share of ERROR rows endorsed by the cross-family peer majority; d = share of CORRECT rows NOT endorsed; NET = (e+d)_T3 - (e+d)_T1

caption: Decomposition of cross-family peer-majority consensus errors by sentence-length tercile (development set E, regime R_AB: 2,672 consensus-scorable rows, 283 sentences; T1/T2/T3 = 98/98/87 sentences with 534/707/569 ERROR and 472/275/115 CORRECT rows). Endorsement rate e (share of ERROR rows the peer majority endorses) falls from 0.29 to 0.04, while divergence rate d (share of CORRECT rows the peer majority does not endorse) rises from 0.31 to 0.91. The dashed line is e + d, and the arrow marks its net degradation from T1 to T3: +0.356 (95% sentence-cluster bootstrap CI [0.198, 0.493]; Δd = +0.608, Δe = −0.252). Error bars are 95% sentence-cluster bootstrap CIs. Replications of this NET test on other populations in later iterations gave smaller or non-significant effects, so this is a development-set lead, not a confirmed finding.
